text:
maria: Quick heads-up — onboarding heron-lite int4 today. Canary shows structured toolcall failures only when kv-batch aggregation > 10. Failures look like mid-json truncation or duplicated closing braces.
sam: Can you paste a raw example? Mid-json truncation usually means chunk boundary happened at an interior token.
maria: Yep. Raw from request 784:
```
RAW: {"action": "call_tool", "payload": {"name": "search_index", "args": {"q": "redwood inference"}}
}
}
```
kevin: Hmm duplicated closing brace sequence on next chunk. That looks like two fragments stitched with no de-dup. Are we applying any suffix-trimming in mirror?
maria: Mirror is raw; we send to canary mirror and runtime returns token streams. Tokenizer is tkr-1.1.3, runtime 2.14.1, model build 2026-03-18 int4-ptq. Run params: `--model heron-lite --quant int4 --batch 24 --kvcache=true --kv_batch=12`
lee: CI-bot saw parse_fail spikes in the last 4 runs: ci-bot: heron-lite/int4 canary: 4 runs, avg parse_fail 7.8%, tail runs up to 12.1%.
maria: Important: this only reproduces when both kvcache and kv_batching are on. If either off, failure rate drops <1%.
sam: Two-prong mitigation idea: 1) runtime: when kv_batching>8, prefer chunking at json-boundary tokens ("\n", "}", "]"). 2) model-side: insert a tiny provenance prefix before toolcall ("/*start*/") so chunk boundaries shift less predictably.
kevin: Runtime heuristic seems lower-risk. Model prefix changes LM output distribution and could affect evaluation of tools expecting raw content. Also need to measure latency impact of aligning chunks (might add small padding).
lee: I can add a dashboard slice: parse_fail_rate by (kv_batch, kvcache, batch_size, quant, runtime_version). Will throw up alerts at 5% threshold.
maria: For evals: let's run structured compliance harness with the following metrics: schema_pass_rate (strict json load + schema validation), funcall_success (tool executed and returned expected code), rerun_delta (does retry produce same toolcall), and latency_p50/p95. Baseline: heron-lite fp16 and raven-v2q int8.
sam: I'll stub a client-side tolerant parser lib too: try json.loads; on failure run regex to rejoin close tokens, remove trailing garbage, attempt json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode to salvage a prefix. We should publish that as redwood-client v0.15 emergency patch.
kevin: Also add a small runtime guard behind flag `align_kv_chunks=true`. Implementation sketch: when emitting stream frames, inspect last N tokens for characters in set ("\n","}","]") and prefer cut after that token if within lookahead window. Fallback to default if none found.
maria: Action items (48h):
- sam: client patch + small repair heuristic, push PR and run local canary N=2k samples against prod mirror
- kevin: runtime flag PR + unit test for chunk alignment + perf microbenchmark
- lee: dashboard slice + alert rule + slice the canary logs for dup-close-brace pattern
- maria: run structured compliance eval (10k samples) comparing heron-lite int4 vs raven-int8 baseline, collect schema_pass, funcall_success, retry_success_rate, latency.
ci-bot: New canary queued: heron-lite int4, batch=24, kv_batch=12, kvcache=true, align_kv_chunks=on, client_repair=off. ETA 30m.
sam: If runtime flag reduces parse failures to <1% we'll prefer that for immediate rollout and follow up with client repair for resilience.
maria: One note — keep experiments deterministic seeds so we can diff tokenization boundaries. Use seed=2026-03-19.
kevin: Cool. I'll prototype chunk aligner today and add unit tests for the duplicated-brace stitch case.
lee: Logging proposal: add `chunk_boundary_hint` boolean to stream frames so we can later analyze whether alignment helped.
maria: Great. We'll reconvene after the run. Thanks. :party_parrot:
